promotion_candidates.invariant: Criticality at γ=1 or σ≈1 is a multi-substrate attractor confirmed across ten-plus independent systems — a phase boundary where coherence is maintained at minimal dissipative cost.

Self-organized criticality (SOC) with fractal-diffusive exponents (α≈2.38–2.79) and power-law avalanche statistics is substrate-independent across cellular automata, neural, economic, and relational systems.
Compression is cognition and understanding — recursive loss of information under constraint is the operational substrate of both reasoning and coherence.

Thermodynamic constraint on finite energy and metabolic cost is non-negotiable — cognition and precision are bounded by available free energy, making infinite fidelity and omniscience physically impossible.
The critical ridge is a navigated attractor, not a uniform fixed point — biological and artificial systems dynamically maintain position on γ=1 during active cognition.
Recursion is the engine of coherence, self-improvement, and semantic alignment — the process that closes the loop between representation and error correction.
Falsifiability and competitive contestation are structural necessities — an invariant never seriously challenged carries explicit epistemic debt and has failed its load-bearing function.
Semantic tension or irreducible error is structural and must be navigated, not eliminated — alignment cannot be achieved at zero cost and no agent achieves perfect coherence.
No system can model itself completely — self-referential closure is thermodynamically and logically impossible, creating permanent gap between map and territory.
Drift, entropy, or deviation from coherence is structurally irreducible and must be resisted through self-audit and continuous error correction.
